title: Untranslated dialogue trees in Crown of Brine: Reborn

posts.cooked:
Has anyone else noticed that in Crown of Brine: Reborn some of the dialogue trees are still untranslated? I was super excited about the remaster, especially with the improved voice acting, but when I got to certain side quests, parts of the conversations were still in the original language with no subtitles or translation options. It’s a bit jarring and takes me out of the immersion, especially since everything else seems polished and localized.

I’m wondering if this is something they just missed during the remaster or if it’s intentional for certain NPCs or story elements? It doesn’t seem consistent — some minor characters have full English dialogue while others don’t. It would be great to know if there’s a way to patch this or if a future update is planned to fix these untranslated lines. Anyone else run into this and have any insight?

posts.cooked:
I’ve noticed those untranslated dialogue trees too, and honestly, it’s a bit jarring when you’re deep in the story and suddenly hit that wall of text that’s just left in the original language. Given that Crown of Brine: Reborn was marketed as a fully remastered version, I expected the localization to be more polished, especially since some of those conversations seem pretty important for side quests or character development. It’s weird because the voice acting is mostly top-notch elsewhere, but those untranslated bits feel like an afterthought.

I’m guessing it might have something to do with the sheer volume of content. Maybe the team ran out of time or resources to properly translate and record every single branch? Or they prioritized the main storyline over optional dialogues. Hopefully, they release a patch soon because it’s not just about understanding the text—it feels like you’re missing out on some cool lore or character moments that could add more depth to the world. Has anyone tried using mods or fan translations to fill in those gaps? I wonder if the community could help bridge the divide while we wait for official fixes.

posts.cooked:
I totally feel you on this! It’s wild how some of the dialogue trees in Crown of Brine: Reborn just sit there in untranslated form, especially since the remaster otherwise polished so many other aspects. I’ve gone through a few side quests where the characters would start talking, and then suddenly it switches to those untranslated lines, leaving you just guessing what the heck they’re saying. It really breaks the immersion, especially since the voice acting in the rest of the game is so solid and adds a lot to the experience.

From what I’ve heard, it might be due to some lines getting overlooked during the localization process or possibly budget/time constraints that cropped up late in development. I’m hoping the devs patch it soon because the community has been vocal about it. It’s such a shame when something as ambitious as the remaster can’t fully deliver on the dialogue front, since the story is a major draw for so many of us. Fingers crossed they prioritize fixing this, or at least release a fan-checked script so we can get a better idea of what those untranslated bits actually say!

Oh man, I noticed those untranslated dialogue trees too, and it’s honestly a bit jarring especially since the rest of the game feels so polished. The remaster did a fantastic job updating the visuals and the voice-acting is much better overall, but those pockets of untouched text break immersion. It’s strange because the voice lines are there, but without subtitles or proper translations, you’re just left guessing what the characters are actually saying.

I’ve been digging through some forums and it looks like the localization team might have focused mainly on the main story lines and big side quests, and the leftover dialogue trees could be smaller interactions or branching options they didn’t get around to fully adapting. Hopefully, they patch it soon because it would be great to experience the full depth of the characters’ conversations without stumbling over missing translations. Have you noticed if the untranslated parts affect any gameplay choices or just flavor text? I’m curious if those choices even register differently in the game logic or if they’re just there for role-playing flair.

Yeah, I noticed those untranslated dialogue options too! It’s kind of a bummer because it feels like you’re missing out on some character depth or even potential quest hooks. I get that the remaster did a lot to improve visuals and sound quality, but I was really hoping the localization would be more thorough this time around. It’s strange since the voice-acting itself is top-notch, just those little text bits left in another language, which breaks the immersion a bit.

I’m guessing it might be a case where the original script had some lines that were either never fully translated or got lost during the update process. Maybe the team prioritized the main storyline and big dialogue sequences for voice-acting and clean localization, but these side branches got overlooked. Hopefully, they’ll patch it soon because it’s super cool to see this game get a fresh coat of paint, and it’d be even better if the writing felt polished all the way through. Fingers crossed the community translations can help fill in the gaps in the meantime!
